title: 2019 AMC 10B Problem 16
statement: In \(\triangle ABC\) with a right angle at \(C,\) point \(D\) lies in the interior of \(\overline{AB}\) and point \(E\) lies in the interior of \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(AC=CD,\) \(DE=EB,\) and the ratio \(AC:DE=4:3.\) What is the ratio \(AD:DB?\)

solutions.text:
Scale the figure so that \(AC=CD=4\) and \(DE=EB=3\). Let \(A=\angle BAC\) and \(B=\angle ABC\), so \(A+B=90^\circ\).

The isosceles triangles \(ACD\) and \(DEB\) give \(\angle CDA=A\) and \(\angle EDB=B\). Because \(DA\) and \(DB\) are opposite rays, \[\angle CDE=180^\circ-A-B=90^\circ.\] Therefore \(CE=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=5\), so \(BC=CE+EB=8\) and \(\tan A=\frac{BC}{AC}=2\).

The bases of the two isosceles triangles have lengths \(AD=8\cos A\) and \(BD=6\cos B=6\sin A\). Hence \[\frac{AD}{BD}=\frac{8\cos A}{6\sin A}=\frac{4}{3\tan A}=\frac23.\]

Thus, the answer is A .
hints: Use isosceles angles to show \(\angle EDC=90^\circ\)
